title: Tag the argument
body: Academic arguments mix claims with the evidence that supports them. Being able to tell them apart is the first step to evaluating a source.
instruction: Choose a category from the palette, then select the matching piece of text. Tag every highlighted span, then press Submit.

_tagCategories.label: Claim
_tagCategories.description: A statement the author asserts to be true.

_tagCategories.label: Evidence
_tagCategories.description: Data or a source offered to support a claim.

_passages.label: Extract from a policy review
_passages.text: The new recycling scheme has been a clear success. Household waste fell by 18% in its first year. Residents also report that it is easy to use.

_taggableSpans.text: The new recycling scheme has been a clear success
_taggableSpans.feedback: Correct - this is the author's overall assertion.
_taggableSpans.feedbackIncorrect: This is the author's headline assertion, so it is a claim rather than evidence.

_taggableSpans.text: Household waste fell by 18% in its first year
_taggableSpans.feedback: Correct - a measured figure offered in support.
_taggableSpans.feedbackIncorrect: A specific measured figure like this is evidence, not a claim.

_taggableSpans.text: Residents also report that it is easy to use
_taggableSpans.feedback: Correct - reported experience used as support.
_taggableSpans.feedbackIncorrect: Reported experience offered in support counts as evidence here.

_passages.label: For comparison (no tagging needed)
_passages.text: Compare the extract above with a neutral description of the same scheme to see how framing changes the reading.

_incorrect.final: Keep trying - check which spans are claims and which are evidence.
_incorrect.notFinal: Not quite. Review your tags and try again.

_partlyCorrect.final: Good work, but not every tag is correct yet.
_partlyCorrect.notFinal: You are on the right track - some tags still need changing.
